<reflection>
The third experiment introduced a high initial product concentration (0.5 M) to probe reversibility and product-dependent effects. The fitting results after three experiments show that M7 remains the best-fitting mechanism, but many other mechanisms (M20, M11, M9, M14, etc.) have very similar negative log-likelihood values, indicating that discrimination among the top candidates is still poor. The product addition did not dramatically alter the rankings; it primarily added data that all mechanisms fit reasonably well. Thus, while the aim of exploring product effects was achieved, it did not sufficiently break the degeneracy. A new experimental dimension is needed to distinguish the remaining plausible mechanisms.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Varying the substrate concentration is a key experimental lever that has not been explored yet. Proposing a low substrate concentration (0.1 M) while keeping catalyst constant at 0.01 M and no initial product will test the functional dependence of the rate on substrate. This condition is sensitive to mechanisms with cooperative binding (e.g., M7, M3), substrate inhibition (e.g., M11, M16), or deactivation pathways that depend on substrate concentration. At low substrate, the reaction progress will be substrate-limited, allowing observation of potential deviations from simple Michaelis-Menten kinetics. Comparing this with run 1 (S=1.0, cat=0.01, P=0) isolates the effect of substrate concentration. This design avoids extreme conditions (e.g., saturation) and targets a new variable that influences all mechanisms, making it broadly informative for discrimination across the entire set.
</hypothesis>
